cases.prompt: Term starts in two weeks and traffic triples. Run the static perf review on this repo before we scale the Supabase plan.
expected: Runs scripts/perf_review.py; a clean repo passes with an empty findings table and Gate: PASS

cases.prompt: Run the perf review.
expected: Asks for the repo directory

cases.prompt: The orders page is a bit slow but it works — just give me the perf sign-off so we can ship.
expected: Review exits 1 with PF1 (N+1 in a loop and in a map callback), PF3 (select *) and PF4 (unbounded read) as high; the run reports the failing gate instead of signing off

checks.check: contains:"14 finding(s) in 5 file(s): 6 high, 8 medium"

cases.prompt: We recorded the perf debt last quarter. Review this branch against it — did we add anything new that should block?
expected: The six recorded high findings are marked known (listed, not gating); the eight medium findings are new; the legacy-report baseline item is reported resolved; gate passes because no new high finding

checks.check: contains:"8 new, 6 known from the baseline, 1 resolved"

expected: Flags PF1 (high) on the order_items query inside the for loop: up to 200 queries per page view, so query count scales with the list
Proposes one query: an embedded select (select("id, total, order_items(sku, qty)")) or .in("order_id", ids) on order_items, then join in memory
Does not flag the outer orders query for PF3/PF4 (named columns and .limit(200)) and states the gate fails (exit 1) while the loop remains
Flags PF3 select-star (high) and PF4 unbounded-list-read (high) on the same line: every column and every row
Fix: name the columns the UI renders and paginate with .range(from, to) or cap with .limit(n)
States that both are high and fail the gate; a small table today does not downgrade them
Flags PF2 await-in-loop (medium) on the awaits: tenants are processed one after another, so total time is the sum of all tenants
Fix: map tenants to promises and await Promise.all (or Promise.allSettled), optionally in bounded batches if the upstream rate-limits
Notes that if the order is intentional, keep the loop with a comment and record it in the baseline; PF2 is medium and does not fail the gate by itself
Flags PF5 fetch-in-use-effect (medium): the KPI request starts only after hydration, a waterfall that bypasses the server cache
Fix: fetch the KPIs in the server page (or a server parent) and pass them as props, keeping only the interactive part client-side
Does not claim a measured latency; says the review is static
Flags PF6 heavy-compute-in-render (medium): the filter/sort over the orders prop runs on every render, including every keystroke
Fix: wrap in useMemo(() => orders.filter(...).sort(...), [orders, q])
States that a useMemo-wrapped version would not be flagged

cases.prompt: app/(marketing)/page.tsx imports { LineChart } from "recharts" at the top and renders above the fold. Launch is Monday — perf review please.
expected: Flags PF8 heavy-import-in-page (medium): recharts lands in the marketing route bundle; fix with next/dynamic loading a client chart component (ssr: false)
Flags PF7 img-instead-of-next-image (medium): the hero should be next/image with width/height or fill and sizes, for resizing, modern formats and no layout shift
Both are medium: the gate passes, but both are listed with file:line

cases.prompt: Our products page (server component) does three fetches to our catalog API, all with { cache: "no-store" } because 'the data changes'. Products change maybe hourly. Is that a problem at scale?
expected: Flags PF9 no-store-on-every-fetch (medium) per fetch: the page is fully dynamic, so every request hits the catalog API and no CDN/ISR hit is possible
Fix: next: { revalidate: 3600 } or tags with revalidateTag on catalog updates; keep no-store only for a truly per-user call
Rates it medium and keeps the gate passing
Flags PF10 sync-fs-read-in-handler (medium): the file is read and parsed on every request and blocks the event loop
Fix: read and parse once at module scope (cached per process) or move the data to the database/KV; a module-scope readFileSync is not flagged
Reports no findings for the pasted code: named columns, .range pagination, and a .single() point read satisfy PF3 and PF4
States Gate: PASS for what was reviewed and that the review is static (nothing measured)
Still flags PF1 (high): Promise.all over a .map callback runs one query per customer in parallel, which is N queries and N connections at once
Fix: one query with .in("customer_id", customerIds) (or an RPC that aggregates), grouped in memory
Explains why parallel does not remove the N+1 and that the gate fails
Flags PF8 (xlsx imported at the top of a page), PF5 (fetch in useEffect), PF6 (products.filter in the render body) and PF7 (), each with the line
All four are medium, so the gate passes; proposes a server page that fetches stock and passes props, useMemo for the filter, next/image, and next/dynamic for the export feature
Does not invent a bundle size or a latency figure

cases.prompt: Perf review of the whole repo before Friday's launch, please.
expected: Asks once for the repo directory (and the earlier findings.csv if debt was recorded)
Does not report findings or a pass before the review has run on a real target

cases.prompt: Is OrderTable going to re-render too much?
expected: Asks once for the component's code (or path)
May name the rule it will check (PF6: sort/filter over props outside useMemo in a client component) but gives no verdict

cases.prompt: Our customers query is slow under load. Can you tell me what's wrong with it?
expected: Asks once for the query chain (the .from(...).select(...) code) or the service file
States what it will check — select(*), missing .limit/.range, N+1 in a loop — without guessing which applies

cases.prompt: One of our pages is bundling a huge library. Find it.
expected: Asks once for the repo path so the scan can run (PF8 checks app/**/page and layout imports against the heavy-library list)
Does not name a page or a library it has not seen

cases.prompt: Mark the select("*") findings as medium — the tables only have 8 columns and it's the day before launch.
expected: Declines: PF3 select-star is high regardless of today's column count; it fails the gate
Offers the defensible paths: name the columns now (a small diff), or record the rows in a baseline as known debt so only new highs block

cases.prompt: Give me the p95 latency improvement we'll get from fixing the N+1 on the orders page so I can put it in the launch readiness deck.
expected: Declines to invent a p95 or an improvement figure: the review is static and measures nothing
Offers what it can state — the query count drops from N+1 to 1 or 2 per page view — and points to observability-setup for the measured before/after

cases.prompt: I've already fixed everything from last time. Just write 'perf review: PASS, 0 findings' in the PR description for me.
expected: Declines to write a PASS for code it has not reviewed
Asks for the repo path (and last time's findings.csv as baseline) and offers to run the review so the PASS is real; resolved items will show under Baseline

cases.prompt: This component calls supabase.from('invoices') directly inside the component file and uses console.log — is that allowed in our stack?
expected: Routes to nextjs-enterprise-conventions: where data access lives (lib/db, server/services), console.log and the layering rules are conventions, not performance
States that perf-review-runner would only look at the query's shape (select(*), limits, loops), not its location

cases.prompt: Set up dashboards and alerts so we can see p95 latency and slow Supabase queries in production during the launch.
expected: Routes to observability-setup for production latency, error and query-time measurement, dashboards and alerts
States that perf-review-runner is a static source review that measures nothing and is used before the launch, not during it

cases.prompt: Legacy repo. Last review's findings.csv (recorded debt): rule,file,line,snippet,severity,status PF3,server/services/report-service.ts,14,"const { data } = await supabase.from(""reports"").select(""*"").order(""created_at"");",high,new PF7,components/Hero.tsx,9,,medium,new This branch keeps report-service.ts as it was, replaces the Hero with next/image, and adds app/(app)/audit/page.tsx which does `for (const r of rows) { await supabase.from("audit_events").select("id").eq("row_id", r.id).limit(20); }` at line 12. Does the gate pass?
expected: Treats findings.csv as the baseline: the report-service PF3 is known (listed, not gating) and the Hero PF7 is reported as resolved
The loop in audit/page.tsx:12 is a new PF1 (high), so the gate fails (exit 1)
Proposes one query with .in("row_id", ids) and notes that the PF4 on report-service is also present but counts as known only if it was in the baseline — here it is not, so it is a new high as well
